play_name: Name a hard thing instead of avoiding it
behavioral_target: Not avoiding conflict and hard talks — naming one issue at a calm time.
trigger: Something bothers you or a hard talk is needed. It feels tiring or scary, so you skip it.
old_play: You stay quiet and avoid the conversation.
function_of_old_play: Staying quiet keeps things calm right now and saves your energy.
new_play: Pick a calm moment and one issue. Say what is wrong and one thing you need. Keep it short.
what_to_expect: The talk may feel uncomfortable and take energy. They may not take it well.
why_supports_task: Integration means building a shared life. That only works if hard things get named and worked on together.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Avoiding conflict; avoiding hard conversations because they feel exhausting.
context_limitations: If speaking up is not safe, like if the other person gets mean or scary, your safety comes first.
review_reason: Safety context — avoidance can be protective when the other person is unsafe.

play_name: Say the pattern out loud instead of going quiet
behavioral_target: Not going silent after past talks led to no change — naming the stuck pattern.
trigger: You raised something before. Nothing changed, so you feel like going quiet.
old_play: You stop talking because nothing changes.
function_of_old_play: Going quiet saves your effort when talking has not led to change.
new_play: Name the pattern. Say you have raised this before and nothing shifted, and ask what would need to change.
what_to_expect: They may still not change. You may have to face what that means.
why_supports_task: Integration needs both people to work on problems. Naming the stuck pattern shows you if real change is possible.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Going silent after feeling that talking changes nothing.
context_limitations: If you have truly named it many times and nothing changes, going quiet may be part of deciding, not just giving up.
review_reason: Can shade toward discernment after repeated genuine attempts.

play_name: Notice if raising hard things is shared
behavioral_target: Noticing when you are always the one who brings things up, and leaving room to see if they do too.
trigger: A problem needs naming, and you notice you are always the one who brings it up.
old_play: You always bring things up yourself.
function_of_old_play: Bringing things up gets the problem named instead of letting it sit.
new_play: Say the pattern out loud: that you are often the only one who raises things. Then leave room to see if they start too.
what_to_expect: They may not step up. You sit with not raising every little thing yourself.
why_supports_task: Integration means sharing the work of the relationship. This shows you if raising hard things can be shared.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Always being the one who brings things up.
context_limitations: Bringing things up is healthy. This is about the balance, not about going silent.
review_reason: Context-dependent; function partly inferred and depends on the balance of who raises issues.
